title: Global extended Čech model and its derived completion unit
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site, $\mathcal O$ a sheaf of commutative rings, and $\mathcal J\subset\mathcal O$ an ideal sheaf locally generated by finitely many sections. Use $D(\mathcal O)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] for the derived category of module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and derived internal Hom [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. An object $E\in D(\mathcal O)$ is locally derived $\mathcal J$-complete if $R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_U}(\mathcal O_U[1/f],E|_U)=0$ for every object $U$ and every $f\in\mathcal J(U)$; here $\mathcal O_U$ denotes the ring sheaf on the slice site and $\mathcal O_U[1/f]$ is sheafified sectionwise localization. $C(\mathcal O_U;f_1,\ldots,f_r)$ denotes the extended alternating localization complex: its degree zero is $\mathcal O_U$, its degree $q$ for $1\leq q\leq r$ is $\prod_{i_1<\cdots<i_q}\mathcal O_U[1/(f_{i_1}\cdots f_{i_q})]$, and all other terms are zero. The differential is the alternating sum of localization maps, and its augmentation to $\mathcal O_U[0]$ is the identity in degree zero and zero in other degrees. For $r=0$ it is $\mathcal O_U[0]$. There exists a complex $K^\bullet$ of $\mathcal O$-modules with a chain map $\epsilon:K^\bullet\to\mathcal O[0]$ such that, whenever $\mathcal J|_U=(f_1,\ldots,f_r)\mathcal O_U$, there is an isomorphism $C(\mathcal O_U;f_1,\ldots,f_r)\cong K|_U$ in $D(\mathcal O_U)$ compatible with augmentations. For any augmented complex having this local description, the natural map $\eta_E:E\cong R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O}(\mathcal O,E)\to R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O}(K,E)$ induced by $\epsilon$ exhibits $R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O}(K,E)$ as the left-adjoint reflection of $E$ into the locally derived $\mathcal J$-complete objects. In particular $\eta_E$ is an isomorphism whenever $E$ is locally derived $\mathcal J$-complete.

proof.text: Give the full subcategory $\mathcal C'$ of objects with finitely many generators the induced coverings. Every object has a covering by these objects, by local finite generation. If $V\to U$ and $U\in\mathcal C\prime$, the restrictions of a finite generating list on $U$ generate $\mathcal J|_V$, so $V\in\mathcal C\prime$. Consequently every covering of an object of $\mathcal C\prime$, and every covering fibre product over that object, already lies in this full subcategory. Give it exactly these coverings. The inclusion preserves coverings and their fibre products, which is continuity as defined in [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology](3); the same covering itself supplies the refinement required for cocontinuity. Faithfulness and fullness hold without refinement because the subcategory is full; cover-density is the first observation. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-special-cocontinuous-sheaf-equivalence]. Its equivalence preserves finite products, so ring operations, module operations, and their equations extend uniquely under its quasi-inverse; this gives an additive equivalence from modules over $\mathcal O$ to modules over its restricted sheaf $u^*\mathcal O$. Equivalences preserve kernels and cokernels, hence complexes, quasi-isomorphisms and augmentations. We may construct $K$ on $\mathcal C'$.

On $\mathcal C'/U$, choose a finitely generated $I\subset\mathcal J(U)$ generating $\mathcal J|_U$. Define the presheaf complex at $V\to U$ to be $K(\mathcal O(V),I\mathcal O(V))$, with restriction maps and augmentation supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-ring-complex-functorial]. Sheafify degreewise; the differential still squares to zero and the augmentation remains a chain map because sheafification is a functor.

For two such ideals $I=(a_1,\ldots,a_s)$ and $I'=(b_1,\ldots,b_t)$, each $a_i$ is locally a sum $\sum_j c_{ij}b_j$ because $I'$ generates the ideal sheaf. Refine the finitely many covers for the $a_i$, and then those expressing each $b_j$ in the $a_i$. On the resulting cover $U_k\to U$ both inclusions of section ideals hold, hence $I\mathcal O(U_k)=I'\mathcal O(U_k)$. On every object over $U_k$ the ring construction has identical inputs and identical maps, so the two presheaf complexes agree there. Their sheafifications are canonically identified by these identities; any two choices agree after the combined refinement, so the identification is unique with this local identity property and satisfies the cocycle identity.

source.place: Tag 099E, paragraph beginning Indeed, if I′.

proof.text: For $V\to U$, the restriction of the presheaf constructed with $I$ is literally the presheaf constructed with $I\mathcal O(V)$. Step 3 identifies its sheafification with the choice for $V$. Both successive restrictions and their composite are locally the identity on the same ring construction, so the identifications satisfy the cocycle condition. Define $K^n(U)=K_U^n(U\xrightarrow{1}U)$ and use these identifications for restriction maps. On a covering the sheaf condition is exactly that of the sheaf $K_U^n$ on $\mathcal C'/U$. The differentials and augmentations agree under restriction and therefore define $K^\bullet\to\mathcal O[0]$. For a chosen list generating $I$, clause (d) of [lem-weil-pbc-ring-complex-functorial] supplies an augmented derived isomorphism over $\mathcal O(U)$. Extend scalars to $\mathcal O_U$: its localization terms become the specified sheafified localizations. The functorial chain maps give a map from this derived scalar extension of $K(\mathcal O(U),I)$ to $K_U$; clause (c), evaluated on every $V\to U$, makes it a quasi-isomorphism after sheafification, using exactness of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-site-module-sheafification-exact]. Thus the desired local Čech isomorphism follows without selecting nonfunctorial isomorphisms independently at every $V$. Return along the module equivalence of Step 1.

For any augmented model as in the statement put $F(E)=R\mathcal Hom(K,E)$ and $\eta_E=\epsilon^*$. On a generating slice, [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-internal-hom-exact-restriction] identifies this with $R\mathcal Hom(C_f,E|_U)$ and its augmentation unit. For a generator $f_i$, [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-localization-rhom-calculus] identifies its derived internal Hom from $\mathcal O_U[1/f_i]$ with $R\mathcal Hom((C_f)_{f_i},E|_U)$. Here $(C_f)_{f_i}$ is contractible: for components indexed by sorted subsets $S$, set $(hx)_S=0$ if $i\in S$, and $(hx)_S=(-1)^{|\{j\in S:j<i\}|}x_{S\cup\{i\}}$ otherwise, using invertibility of $f_i$ to identify the localizations. In $dh+hd$ the term deleting $i$ is $x_S$; terms deleting any other index cancel in pairs with opposite signs. Thus $dh+hd=1$, including degree zero. The internal Hom vanishes for each generator on every further slice. By [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-derived-complete-elements-ideal] its vanishing sections form an ideal sheaf, hence contain every section of $\mathcal J$. This proves completeness of $F(E)$. For the empty list the complex and unit are the identity, and localization at zero is zero.

If $L$ is complete, each nonempty product $g=\prod_{i\in S}f_i$ belongs to $\mathcal J(U)$, so $R\mathcal Hom(\mathcal O_U[1/g],L|_U)=0$. The kernel $A_f$ of $C_f\to\mathcal O_U[0]$ has only the positive-degree localization terms. Explicitly, let $F^pA_f$ be the subcomplex with the terms of $A_f$ in degrees $\geq p$ and zero below $p$, for $1\leq p\leq r+1$. Then $F^1A_f=A_f$, $F^{r+1}A_f=0$, and $F^pA_f/F^{p+1}A_f=A_f^p[-p]$, a finite sum of localizations shifted by $-p$. The degreewise split short exact sequences give distinguished triangles. Exactness of internal Hom [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-internal-hom-exact-restriction] applied successively to this filtration gives $R\mathcal Hom(A_f,L|_U)=0$. Applying it to $A_f\to C_f\to\mathcal O_U$ proves that $\eta_L|_U$ is an isomorphism. The cone of $\eta_L$ has zero cohomology on a generating cover, so its cohomology sheaves vanish globally and $\eta_L$ is an isomorphism.

Let $Z_E$ be the cone of $\eta_E$. On a generating slice the triangle in Step 6 gives $Z_E|_U\cong R\mathcal Hom(A_f,E|_U)$. Applying contravariant internal Hom to the successive triangles of the explicit filtration in Step 6 expresses this object by finitely many distinguished triangles whose other terms are shifts of $M_g=R\mathcal Hom(\mathcal O_U[1/g],E|_U)$ for nonempty products $g$. A Hom-complex representative $\mathcal Hom^\bullet(\mathcal O_U[1/g],I^\bullet)$, with $I^\bullet$ K-injective, has a termwise $\mathcal O_U[1/g]$-action by precomposition; hence localization tensoring fixes it. Localization is flat (sectionwise localization preserves exact sequences and sheafification is exact by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-site-module-sheafification-exact]), so also $M_g\otimes^{\mathbf L}\mathcal O_U[1/g]\cong M_g$. For complete $L$, the tensor/internal-Hom identity of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-internal-hom-exact-restriction] gives
$$R\mathcal Hom(M_g,L|_U)\cong R\mathcal Hom(M_g\otimes^{\mathbf L}\mathcal O_U[1/g],L|_U)\cong R\mathcal Hom(M_g,R\mathcal Hom(\mathcal O_U[1/g],L|_U))=0.$$
Applying internal Hom into $L|_U$ to those triangles and inducting from the zero end implies $R\mathcal Hom(Z_E|_U,L|_U)=0$. Slice compatibility of the same calculus node makes this the restriction of $R\mathcal Hom(Z_E,L)$; its cohomology sheaves vanish on a cover and hence globally. Applying internal Hom into $L$ to $E\to F(E)\to Z_E$ now gives an isomorphism $R\mathcal Hom(F(E),L)\to R\mathcal Hom(E,L)$. Taking zeroth derived global sections using [lem-pur-rhom-global-sections] gives the required bijection $\operatorname{Hom}(F(E),L)\to\operatorname{Hom}(E,L)$, induced by composition with $\eta_E$. Naturality follows from the internal-Hom functor and the fixed augmentation. Together with Step 5 this proves the left adjoint for every augmented model with the stated local description.
